newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring wheat bids mixed.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - Spring wheat bids mixed.

text.p: Bids for dark northern spring wheat were mixed on Monday with eastern locations tacking on a premium due to concerns of weather-related crop losses, several cash grain dealers said.
Scab has been reported in parts of Minnesota and North Dakota. The fungus, which thrives in wet conditions, can cause yield losses.
The weather turned hot and dry across much of Minnesota on Monday which should improve conditions but the soil remained excessively wet, according to the Minnesota Agricultural Statistics Service.
Scab has also been of concern in parts of North Dakota but a dealer there said the extent of the damage would not be clear until harvest begins in two to three weeks.

In Montana, some irrigated winter wheat north of Billings was already harvested, a Montana merchandiser said. Winter wheat protein content was about 11.5 to 12.5 percent and yields were looking good, the merchandiser said.
White wheat bids were a shade lower and activity was quiet as the market awaited results of Pakistan's 500,000-tonne tender, dealers said.
